issues.legal_issue: Governmental requisition of property for public purposes constitutes acquisition in the broader sense used by the court-fee provision when it deprives the owner of possession while leaving title with the owner.
material_facts: The property was requisitioned for a public purpose and remained in governmental possession through successive extensions of the requisition period.
The owner retained title, while the Government had possession of the property.
The compensation dispute arose from the continued requisition of the property.
issues.conclusion: Requisitioning in these circumstances constitutes acquisition for the purpose of the court-fee provision concerning appeals about compensation for acquisition of property for public purposes.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 to 6 of the Requisitioning and Acquisition of Immovable Property Act, 1952 concern requisitioning, while section 7 concerns acquisition of requisitioned property; however, acquisition is not confined to transfer of title. Deprivation of possession for an extended or indefinite period can itself amount to acquisition. The Court relied on State of West Bengal v. Subodh Gopal Bose and Dwarkadas Shrinivas of Bombay v. The Sholapur Spinning & Weaving Co. Ltd., which treated acquisition broadly, and referred to The Minister of State for the Army v. Dalziel. It also noted that requisitioning laws had to comply with Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 of the Constitution when those provisions were in force.

rule.if: compensation_appeal and public_purpose_use and government_possession and owner_retains_title and prolonged_deprivation_of_possession

predicates.compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal arising from a dispute about compensation for property taken or held by the government.
predicates.public_purpose_use: The government uses or holds the property for a public purpose.
predicates.government_possession: The government has possession of the property.
predicates.owner_retains_title: The owner retains title to the property despite the government's possession.
predicates.prolonged_deprivation_of_possession: The owner has been deprived of possession for an extended or indefinite period.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal concerns government possession for public purposes that has deprived an owner of possession for an extended or indefinite period, the requisition counts as acquisition even if the owner retains title.

issues.legal_issue: A binding award determining compensation made by a statutory authority is an order relating to compensation, even if it is not an order of a civil court.
material_facts: A statutory arbitrator determined the compensation payable for the requisitioned property.
The award formally expressed the arbitrator's decision and bound the parties.
The owners appealed against the award under the applicable statutory appeal provision.
issues.conclusion: The arbitrator's award is an order relating to compensation within the meaning of the court-fee provision.
issues.legal_principle: Section 51 of the Tamil Nadu Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1955 refers to an order relating to compensation under an enactment concerning acquisition for public purposes. Under section 3 of that Act, definitions apply unless the context otherwise requires; section 3(iv) refers to meanings in the Code of Civil Procedure where applicable, and section 2(14) of that Code defines an order as the formal expression of a civil court's decision. In the context of section 51, however, the order need not be made by a civil court and may be made by a statutory authority. The Court relied on Sahadu Gangaram Bhagade v. Special Deputy Collector, which treated an arbitrator's award as a formal, binding decision, and approved the reasoning in In re Ananda Lal Chakrabutty and C.B.G. Trust v. Union of India.

rule.if: compensation_appeal and statutory_authority_decides_compensation and award_formally_expresses_decision and award_binds_parties and property_taken_for_public_purpose

predicates.compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal arising from a dispute about compensation for property taken or held by the government.
predicates.statutory_authority_decides_compensation: An authority empowered by law determines the compensation payable for the property.
predicates.award_formally_expresses_decision: The authority's award formally states its decision.
predicates.award_binds_parties: The award binds the parties to the compensation proceeding.
predicates.property_taken_for_public_purpose: The property is taken or held for a public purpose.

issues.definition: When a statutory authority formally decides compensation for property taken for a public purpose and its decision binds the parties, the award qualifies as a compensation order in the appeal.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal challenging a statutory arbitrator's compensation award for property requisitioned for a public purpose attracts ad valorem court fee rather than the fixed fee under the residuary provision.
material_facts: The owners appealed under section 11 of the Requisitioning and Acquisition of Immovable Property Act, 1952 against an arbitrator's award determining compensation for requisitioned property.
The owners claimed a higher amount of compensation than the amount awarded and disputed the difference in the appeal.
The property was held by the Government for a public purpose.
issues.conclusion: Court fee is payable ad valorem on the difference between the compensation awarded and the amount claimed; the residuary fixed-fee provision does not apply.
issues.legal_principle: Section 51 of the Tamil Nadu Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1955 provides that the fee on a memorandum of appeal against an order relating to compensation under an enactment for acquisition of property for public purposes is computed on the difference between the amount awarded and the amount claimed. Read with Article 1 of Schedule I, it requires ad valorem court fee. Article 3(iii)(A)(1)(a) of Schedule II, the residuary fixed-fee provision, is not attracted. The Court applied its conclusions on the broad meaning of acquisition and on a statutory arbitrator's award being an order, relying particularly on Sahadu Gangaram Bhagade v. Special Deputy Collector.

rule.if: compensation_award_appeal and property_taken_for_public_purpose and appeal_seeks_difference_between_award_and_claim and award_formally_expresses_decision and award_binds_parties

predicates.compensation_award_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an award that determines compensation for property taken or held by the government.
predicates.property_taken_for_public_purpose: The property is taken or held for a public purpose.
predicates.appeal_seeks_difference_between_award_an: The appellant seeks compensation beyond the amount awarded and disputes the difference between the two amounts.
predicates.award_formally_expresses_decision: The authority's award formally states its decision.
predicates.award_binds_parties: The award binds the parties to the compensation proceeding.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a binding, formal compensation award for property taken for a public purpose and seeks the difference between the award and the amount claimed, ad valorem court fee applies and the residuary fixed fee does not.
